title: Implement forEach
description: Implement a function myForEach(arr, callback) that calls the callback with (element, index, array) for every element, just like Array.prototype.forEach. Return undefined.
whatShouldHappen: Loop through the array from index 0 to the last index.
Call the callback with three arguments: the current element, the current index, and the original array.
Do not collect or return any values — forEach always returns undefined.
patternExplanation: forEach is a loop in disguise — it delegates what to do per element to a callback, separating iteration from behavior. Re-implementing it reveals exactly what the native version does.

title: Implement map
description: Implement myMap(arr, callback) that returns a new array where each element is the result of calling callback(element, index, array), just like Array.prototype.map.
whatShouldHappen: Create an empty result array.
Loop through each element.
Push the return value of callback(element, index, array) into the result.
Return the result array — never modify the original array.
patternExplanation: map collects callback return values into a new array — it never modifies the original. Building it from scratch cements the difference between forEach (side effects) and map (new array).

title: Implement Array.prototype.flat
description: Implement a recursive/iterative array flattening function that flattens nested arrays up to the specified depth (default 1) without using Array.prototype.flat.
whatShouldHappen: Default depth to 1 if undefined.
If depth <= 0, return a copy of arr.
Iterate through elements of arr: if an element is an array, recursively flatten it with depth - 1 and push unpacked items to result.
If not an array, push directly to result.
Return result.
patternExplanation: Polyfilling Array.prototype.flat demonstrates recursion depth control and dynamic array concatenation.

title: Custom Array Filter
description: Implement a custom filter function that returns a new array with all elements that pass the test implemented by the provided callback function fn(element, index, array) without using Array.prototype.filter.
whatShouldHappen: Initialize filtered array = [].
Loop through arr from index 0 to arr.length - 1.
Invoke callback(arr[i], i, arr).
If the return value is truthy, push arr[i] into filtered array.
Return filtered array.
patternExplanation: Implementing functional array iteration primitives reinforces the underlying mechanics of higher-order JavaScript functions.

title: Custom Array Reduce
description: Implement a custom reduce function that executes a user-supplied reducer callback function on each element of the array, in order, passing in the return value from the calculation on the preceding element.
whatShouldHappen: Check if array is empty and initialValue is undefined; throw TypeError.
If initialValue is provided, set accumulator = initialValue, startIndex = 0.
Otherwise, accumulator = arr[0], startIndex = 1.
Loop from startIndex through array, setting accumulator = callback(accumulator, arr[i], i, arr).
Return accumulator.

traceTable.inputLabel: arr = [1, 2, 3, 4], callback = (acc, x) => acc + x, initialValue = 0

patternExplanation: Understanding how reduce folds state sequentially across iterations is fundamental for building transducers and state pipelines.

title: Chunk Array into Subarrays
description: Given an array arr and a chunk size size, return a chunked array consisting of subarrays each of maximum length size.
whatShouldHappen: Initialize chunked = [].
Loop with step size: for (let i = 0; i < arr.length; i += size).
Slice subarray arr.slice(i, i + size) and push to chunked.
Return chunked.
patternExplanation: Advancing the loop counter by arbitrary stride k enables batching array streams efficiently.
